questions.explanation: A switch dispatches on equality between its selector and each case label, and a case label has to be a compile-time constant, so a two-sided band such as month >= 3 && month <= 5 cannot be written as a label at all. A ladder is the right construct whenever a branch tests a comparison or a compound expression instead of one fixed value, which is exactly what both seasonal bands do. Reading the first switch option assumes a label can hold a comparison; the second assumes a switch compares against a range; the last confuses control flow with dispatch.
questions.hint: Ask whether a case label could ever hold a comparison between two variables.
questions.learningObjective: choose a ladder over a switch for branches that test two-sided compound ranges

options.text: An else-if chain, because a case label cannot hold a comparison at all

options.misconception: believes a switch can compare its selector against a range of values
options.text: A switch, because each band can be keyed by its first month number

options.misconception: believes a case label accepts a compound comparison expression
options.text: A switch on the month, because a switch can test compound comparisons

options.misconception: believes a switch is unusable here because the bands are two-sided ranges
options.text: A for loop with a break, because a switch cannot express two-sided ranges

questions.explanation: A rewrite preserves the classifier only if it maps every one of the tested inputs to the same band as the reference, and each candidate has to be traced in its own order. The reference gives L, M, H for 5, 15 and 25. A verbatim copy gives the same sequence, and restating the bands from the top down also gives L, M, H. The reversed-order version tests v < 20 first, so 15 is labelled L and the sequence becomes L, L, H, which is wrong even though its two bounds are the same two numbers. The two-branch version prints L, M, M and so fails on 25.
questions.hint: Trace all three inputs through each rewrite before judging it.
questions.learningObjective: judge which rewrites of a band classifier preserve its output on a set of inputs

options.text: a verbatim copy of the reference chain, with the same two bounds in the same order

options.misconception: believes the values tested here all fall inside the two bands the shorter chain keeps
options.text: a two-branch chain that drops the top band entirely and keeps only L and M

options.misconception: believes reversing the order of two disjoint bounds leaves the mapping unchanged
options.text: the same two bounds with the wider test written first, so 20 and up is tested for first
the bands restated from the top down as v >= 20, then v >= 10, then the low band

questions.stem:
The reference classifier prints L, M, H for the inputs 5, 15 and 25. Which rewrites print that same sequence? Select every one that does.
reference: if (v < 10) band = "L"; else if (v < 20) band = "M"; else band = "H";
